section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the true concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace" involves the complete nullification of the opposing force through the revelation of Yechidah, unlike the level of Chayah which only overcomes it.
section.t: And it can be said,
that in this manner it is also regarding the concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
that it contains
(an analogy of)
these three levels.
And the explanation is,
that the true essence of the concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
where the opposing force is completely nullified,
as explained above
(section 2)
from the discourse of the Master of the Redemption,
is through the revelation of Yechidah.
For the level of Chayah,
since there is an opposing force against it,
therefore its revelation does not negate and completely nullify the alien desires of the animal soul,
and it is only that the desire for G-dliness
(of the level of Chayah)
overpowers the desires of the animal soul.
And in order for there to be a nullification of the desires of the animal soul, it is through the revelation of Yechidah.
For since the level of Yechidah has no opposing force against it,
the faintest reflection of it they do not have,
therefore through the revelation of Yechidah the opposing force is nullified automatically.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section states that the true "redemption in peace" will be specifically at the coming of Moshiach, who is the Yechidah of all of Hishtalshelus, yet it is drawn down through our service now, as exemplified by King Dovid.
section.t: And this is that the true essence of the concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace" will be specifically at the coming of Moshiach,
for just as in a person,
the nullification of his opposing force is specifically through the revelation of Yechidah,
so too is it regarding the entirety of the world,
that specifically through Moshiach,
who is the Yechidah of the entirety of Hishtalshelus,
will the sitra achara be completely nullified.
However, nevertheless,
since all the revelations of the future depend on our deeds and service now,
also the concept of the nullification of the sitra achara through the revelation of the general Yechidah that will be in the future,
is through a person revealing the Yechidah within him, through which the alien desires of his animal soul are nullified.
And in particular,
when through the revelation of his Yechidah he also effects
(to a degree)
the nullification of the sitra achara in another.
And like King Dovid,
that through his service he effected that even Amasai said to him, "Peace, peace to you and peace to your helpers,"
and that even the men of Avshalom prayed for Dovid's victory.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contrasts the limited revelation of Yechidah now with the unlimited future redemption, explaining that the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev, being connected to the Yechidah of Torah, is without measure or limitation.
section.t: And now, since all matters are in limitation,
therefore,
also the matter of mesiras nefesh that stems from the revelation of Yechidah
is regarding a limited matter.
[And in the manner explained above
(section 7)
regarding the revelation of the power of Ein Sof in procreation,
that the revelation of Ein Sof is in a limited matter].
And from this it is understood,
that although the revelation of the general Yechidah of the future is through the revelation of Yechidah now,
nevertheless,
the revelation of Yechidah now compared to the revelation of the general Yechidah of the future is incomparable.
And so too is it regarding the "He redeemed my soul in peace" that occurred by Dovid,
for since his redemption in peace was only regarding a few people
(Amasai,
the men of Avshalom, etc.)
and not regarding the entirety of the world
(for in the entirety of the world there were opponents),
therefore,
it is utterly incomparable to the redemption in peace of the future,
which will have no limitations.
And the drawing down of the redemption in peace of the future
(without limit)
through the redemption in peace of Dovid
(which is regarding limited matters)
is in the manner of the drawing down of the matter of walking and the unlimited through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos in this world by those who engage only in the revealed aspect of Torah.
And the concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace" in the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev
[and likewise in the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz],
since the redemption is regarding the inner dimension of Torah,
the Yechidah of Torah,
therefore,
the concept of "He redeemed my soul in peace" in this redemption,
has no measures or limitations,
and it is regarding all matters.
